mainInsight: Values are positive, so (a - 1)(b - 1) is maximised by the two largest numbers: find the top two (a min-heap of size 2, sorting, or two variables).
canonicalApproach: Track the two largest in a pass

approaches.name: Track the two largest in a pass

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; two variables are simpler than a heap.

promptVariants: Which two elements maximise the product for positive numbers?
What does a size-2 min-heap hold?
cards.explanation: For positive values the product (a-1)(b-1) is increasing in both a and b.

promptVariants: Why is the answer determined by the two largest values only?
Why does the -1 not change the choice?
cards.answer: Subtracting 1 from each factor is a monotone shift: for positive integers (a-1)(b-1) increases with a and with b, so the two largest values give the maximum.
cards.explanation: Negative values would change this (see Maximum Product of Three Numbers).

promptVariants: Time complexity of the size-2 heap solution: ___
Complete the statement: Time complexity of the size-2 heap solution: ___
cards.explanation: n pushes/pops on a heap bounded by 2 (constant cost each).
The heap never holds more than 3 items.

promptVariants: Why is the answer `(heap[0]-1)*(heap[1]-1)` after the loop?
What do heap[0] and heap[1] contain?
cards.answer: After processing all numbers the heap holds the two largest values (the smallest of the three is popped each time). heap[0] is the smaller of the two and heap[1] the larger (for a size-2 heap the order is irrelevant for the product). The product is symmetric.
cards.explanation: Two variables avoid the heap entirely.
The two largest are 9 and 6, so (9-1) * (6-1) = 40.

incorrectOptionExplanations.54: That forgets to subtract 1 from each factor (9 * 6).
incorrectOptionExplanations.24: That pairs 9 with 4 ((9-1) * (4-1)); the two largest values give more.
incorrectOptionExplanations.8: That pairs 9 with the smallest value ((9-1) * (2-1)).
